back: Cl⁻ < Br⁻ < I⁻: larger ion, outer electrons further from nucleus and more shielded, more easily lost.
AgCl white, dissolves in dilute NH₃. AgBr cream, dissolves in concentrated NH₃. AgI pale yellow, insoluble.
NaCl + H₂SO₄ → NaHSO₄ + HCl (steamy fumes; no redox).
NaBr + H₂SO₄ → NaHSO₄ + HBr; 2HBr + H₂SO₄ → Br₂ + SO₂ + 2H₂O (S +6 → +4).
HI reduces H₂SO₄ to SO₂, S (6HI + H₂SO₄ → 3I₂ + S + 4H₂O) and H₂S (8HI + H₂SO₄ → 4I₂ + H₂S + 4H₂O).
Steamy fumes (HI), purple fumes/black solid (I₂), yellow solid (S), bad-egg smell (H₂S).

front: Why acidify with HNO₃ before Ag⁺
back: Removes carbonate; nitric acid adds no halide ions (HCl would give AgCl).

front: Oxidation states of S reached with halides
back: Cl⁻: none (+6). Br⁻: +4 (SO₂). I⁻: +4, 0 and −2 (SO₂, S, H₂S).
